hints: Notice the two battery symbols face opposite ways round the single loop, so the $12.0 \text{ V}$ source drives current one way and the $8.0 \text{ V}$ source drives it the other way.
Connect this to net e.m.f. for opposing sources: subtract the smaller e.m.f. from the larger e.m.f. to find the resultant voltage round the loop.
Add the two series resistances $1.0 \Omega$ and $0.5 \Omega$, then use $I = V/R$ with the net $4.0 \text{ V}$ to find $I$ in $\text{A}$.
walkthrough: Identify the loop: the $12.0 \text{ V}$ source with $1.0 \Omega$ is in series with the $8.0 \text{ V}$ source with $0.5 \Omega$, forming one complete circuit.
Decide aiding or opposing: going round the loop the polarities are opposite, so the resultant e.m.f. is the difference $V = 12.0 - 8.0 = 4.0 \text{ V}$ in the direction of the larger source.
Calculate and check units: $I = 2.666... \text{ A} \approx 2.7 \text{ A}$, with $\text{V}/\Omega = \text{A}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Net e.m.f. $12.0 - 8.0 = 4.0 \text{ V}$ across total $1.5 \Omega$ gives $I = 4.0/1.5 = 2.7 \text{ A}$.

B.explanation: Uses net $4.0 \text{ V}$ but divides by only the $1.0 \Omega$ resistance, ignoring the $0.5 \Omega$ resistance.

C.explanation: Uses the $8.0 \text{ V}$ e.m.f. alone with $1.0 \Omega$, ignoring that the two sources oppose each other.

D.explanation: Adds the e.m.f.s to $20 \text{ V}$, treating the $12.0 \text{ V}$ and $8.0 \text{ V}$ sources as aiding instead of opposing.
